Examples

Pushing Surplus from Your Own POS

This guide shows how to push surplus items directly from your own POS or inventory system to Karma, so they appear in the app for customers to purchase at a discount.

See it work — interactive demo

A self-contained walkthrough of this whole integration: push surplus from a mock POS, watch it appear in the Karma app, buy as a guest, and see the order.created and tab.payment_completed webhooks arrive back in your POS — every request and event shown live on the wire.

View demo →

Overview

Surplus is food that would otherwise go to waste at the end of a service — pastries left over after the lunch rush, hot food approaching close-of-day, or excess prep. By pushing surplus to Karma you:

  • Sell more and reduce food waste in a single step
  • Control quantity, discount, and sell-by window from your own system
  • Keep Karma's inventory in sync with your real-world stock

How It Works

The helper endpoint POST /api/v1/locations/:locationId/helpers/surplus/add handles everything in one call:

  1. Find or create the item — pass an externalId (your SKU or internal ID) and full item details. Karma looks up the item by externalId for this location. If it doesn't exist yet, it creates it automatically.
  2. Set the sell window — pass a single date (midnight → store closing time) or an explicit validFrom/validUntil range.
  3. Upsert the surplus entry — if you already pushed surplus for this item today, the quantity is replaced with the new value. Pushing again at 3 pm with quantity: 3 means there are now 3 left — not 3 more.

Prerequisites

  • A Karma API key with surplus:create permission scoped to your location
  • Your location ID (available in the Karma Merchant dashboard under Settings → Integrations)
  • Available category tag keys (see GET /api/v1/category-tags)
  • Available allergen tag keys (same endpoint, filter by type ALLERGEN)

Quick Example

Install the SDK or use plain fetch — both are shown below.

Code
npm install @karmalicious/karma-api-js

Response (201 Created — first time this item appears as surplus today):

Code
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": {
    "surplusEntry": {
      "id": 88421,
      "itemId": 56789,
      "locationId": 1234,
      "ministock": 5,
      "validFrom": "2024-12-20T00:00:00.000Z",
      "validUntil": "2024-12-20T21:00:00.000Z",
      "discountPercentage": 50,
      "overridePriceCents": null,
      "note": null,
      "createdAt": "2024-12-20T14:32:10.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2024-12-20T14:32:10.000Z"
    },
    "item": {
      "id": 56789,

    }
  },

    "requestId": "req_abc123",
    "timestamp": "2024-12-20T14:32:10.000Z",

item.created: true means the inventory item was newly created. On subsequent calls for the same externalId, it will be false.

Request Reference

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
itemIdintegereither/orExisting Karma item ID. Use if you've already created items via the inventory API.
itemobjecteither/orItem definition for find-or-create. Mutually exclusive with itemId.
item.externalIdstringyes (with item)Your system's stable identifier for this product (SKU, PLU, barcode). Used for idempotent lookups.
item.titlestringyes (with item)Product name shown to customers.
item.descriptionstringnoShort product description.
item.imageUrlstringnoPublicly accessible image URL.
item.basePriceCentsintegeryes (with item)Full (non-discounted) price in cents, e.g. 12900 for 129 SEK.
item.categorystringnoExisting category tag key. See GET /api/v1/category-tags.
item.allergensstring[]noExisting allergen tag keys. See GET /api/v1/category-tags?type=ALLERGEN.
quantityinteger ≥ 1yesNumber of surplus items available. Replaces any existing quantity for this item/date.
discountPercentageinteger 50–90noDiscount off basePriceCents. E.g. 50 = half price.
overridePriceCentsinteger ≥ 0noFixed surplus price in cents. Mutually exclusive with discountPercentage.
notestringnoInternal note (not customer-facing).
datestringeither/orISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Sell window is midnight → store closing time.
validFromstringeither/orISO date or datetime for start of sell window.
validUntilstringnoISO date or datetime for end of sell window.

Scenario Walkthroughs

End-of-day push from POS

Your POS runs a nightly job at 19:00 that checks remaining stock and pushes anything above a threshold to Karma:

Code
import { createKarmaClient } from '@karmalicious/karma-api-js'

const client = createKarmaClient({ apiKey: process.env.KARMA_API_KEY!, locationId: 1234 })

async function pushEndOfDaySurplus() {
  const remaining = await pos.getRemainingStock() // your POS API
  const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10) // "2024-12-20"

  for (const item of remaining.filter(i => i.quantity >= 2 && i.expiresAfterToday)) {
    await client.surplus.add({
      item: {
        externalId: item.sku,
        title: item.name,
        description: item.description,
        imageUrl: item.imageUrl,
        basePriceCents: Math.round(item.priceSEK * 100),
        category: mapCategory(item.category),
        allergens: item.allergens,
      },
      quantity: item.quantity,
      discountPercentage: 50,
      date: today,
    })
  }
}

function mapCategory(posCategory: string): string {
  const map: Record<string, string> = {
    'hot-food': 'FOOD',
    'bakery':   'BAKERY',
    'drinks':   'BEVERAGE',
  }
  return map[posCategory] ?? 'FOOD'
}

Updating quantity mid-day

You already pushed 10 items at open. At noon, 4 have sold via Karma and 3 more via in-store. Push the updated count — Karma replaces the quantity:

The response will be 200 OK (not 201) — the entry was updated, not created.

Bulk Upload (High-Volume Integrations)

For integrations that push many products at once — grocery chains, large venue systems, or any automated nightly sync — the bulk endpoint lets you send up to 500 items in a single call. It has the same item find-or-create logic as the single endpoint; the main difference is that errors are per-item — one bad entry doesn't abort the rest.

Response (207 Multi-Status):

Code
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": {
    "results": [
      { "index": 0, "surplusId": 88421, "itemId": 56789, "itemCreated": true,  "surplusCreated": true },
      { "index": 1, "surplusId": 88422, "itemId": 56790, "itemCreated": false, "surplusCreated": true }
    ],
    "errors": []
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "req_abc123",
    "timestamp": "2024-12-20T14:32:10.000Z",
    "executionTimeMs": 312
  }
}

If some items fail, status becomes "partial" and the failures are listed under errors — the successful items are still created:

Code
{
  "status": "partial",
  "data": {
    "results": [
      { "index": 0, "surplusId": 88421, "itemId": 56789, "itemCreated": true, "surplusCreated": true }
    ],
    "errors": [
      { "index": 1, "error": "Provide either date or validFrom" }
    ]
  }
}

Migration from karma-api (Semafor/ICA integration)

If you were previously calling the legacy karma-api service, here is the field mapping to the new bulk endpoint:

Old karma-api fieldNew fieldNotes
integration_item_iditem.externalIdSame stable product ID — keep it unchanged
titleitem.title
base_priceitem.basePriceCentsSame unit (öre / pence / cents)
discount_percentagediscountPercentageMinimum is now 50 (was 40 with loyalty)
numquantity
expiry_date (YYYY-MM-DD)dateSame format
image_urlitem.imageUrl
gtinnot a dedicated fieldPass as part of your externalId or omit

The old two-step flow (POST /items then POST /sales/items) collapses into a single call per item (or one bulk call). No separate "create sale" step is needed.

Limits and behaviour

  • Maximum 500 items per request
  • Items are processed sequentially — one failure does not affect subsequent items
  • Uses the same upsert semantics as the single endpoint: if surplus for this externalId already exists on the given date, the quantity is replaced
  • Requires surplus:create permission on your API key (same as the single endpoint)

Fetching Available Tag Keys

Before you can set category or allergens, look up the tag keys your Karma account has configured:

Code
# All category tags
curl "https://common-api.karma.life/api/v1/category-tags" \
  -H "X-API-Key: karma_live_your_key_here"

# Allergen tags only
curl "https://common-api.karma.life/api/v1/category-tags?type=ALLERGEN" \
  -H "X-API-Key: karma_live_your_key_here"

Common examples:

KeyMeaning
FOODGeneral food
BEVERAGEDrinks
BAKERYBaked goods
GLUTENContains gluten
MILKContains milk / dairy
NUTSContains nuts
EGGContains egg
FISHContains fish

Error Handling

HTTP statusWhen it happensWhat to do
400 Bad RequestMissing required field, both itemId and item provided, both discountPercentage and overridePriceCents setFix the request body per the error message
401 UnauthorizedMissing or invalid API keyCheck your X-API-Key header
403 ForbiddenAPI key lacks surplus:create permission for this locationContact Karma support to update key permissions
404 Not FounditemId not found at this locationVerify the item ID and location ID
500 Internal Server ErrorServer-side errorRetry with exponential backoff; contact Karma if persistent

Best Practices

Keep externalId stable

The externalId is how Karma maps your POS product to its internal item. Use a stable identifier (SKU, PLU, barcode) — never a name or timestamp. Changing the externalId creates a duplicate item.

Push quantities, not deltas

Always push the current absolute quantity remaining, not how many you want to add. If you have 8 left, push quantity: 8. Karma replaces the number, so pushing twice with 5 leaves you with 5 — not 10.

Set discountPercentage at 50 % minimum

The Karma platform enforces a minimum 50 % discount on surplus items. Using overridePriceCents bypasses the percentage calculation but still represents a meaningful saving for customers.

Automate the push, then let webhooks handle sold-out

Subscribe to the surplus.sold_out webhook to know when Karma customers have bought all available units — then stop serving that item from your POS too if needed.

Code
# Subscribe to surplus events
curl -X POST "https://common-api.karma.life/api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions" \
  -H "X-API-Key: karma_live_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://your-pos-system.example.com/webhooks/karma",
    "events": ["surplus.sold_out", "surplus.added"],
    "secret": "your-webhook-secret"
  }'

Listing Your Surplus

Use GET /api/v1/locations/:locationId/helpers/surplus to see everything you've pushed — past, active, and future — with each item's externalId included so you can map entries back to your own product IDs.

Code
# All surplus for this location
curl "https://common-api.karma.life/api/v1/locations/1234/helpers/surplus" \
  -H "X-API-Key: karma_live_your_key_here"

# Filter to a specific date range
curl "https://common-api.karma.life/api/v1/locations/1234/helpers/surplus?from=2024-12-20&to=2024-12-22" \
  -H "X-API-Key: karma_live_your_key_here"

Response:

  "data": {

        "id": 88421,

        "discountPercentage": 50,
        "overridePriceCents": null,
        "computedPriceCents": 6450,

        "status": "active",
        "createdAt": "2024-12-20T14:32:10.000Z",
        "updatedAt": "2024-12-20T14:32:10.000Z",
        "item": {
          "id": 56789,
          "externalId": "sku-pasta-bolognese",
          "name": "Pasta Bolognese",
          "description": "Classic slow-cooked bolognese with tagliatelle",
          "imageUrl": "https://your-cdn.example.com/pasta-bolognese.jpg",

        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Each entry has a computed status:

ValueMeaning
upcomingvalidFrom is in the future — not yet visible to customers
activeCurrently within the sell window
expiredvalidUntil has passed

Syncing with your POS display

Code
import { createKarmaClient } from '@karmalicious/karma-api-js'

const client = createKarmaClient({ apiKey: process.env.KARMA_API_KEY!, locationId: 1234 })

async function getSurplusByExternalId() {
  const entries = await client.surplus.list()

  // Key by your own product ID for easy lookup
  return new Map(
    entries
      .filter(e => e.item.externalId)
      .map(e => [e.item.externalId!, { surplusId: e.id, quantity: e.ministock, status: e.status }])
  )
}

Editing and Deleting Surplus

Once you have a surplus entry's id (from the list or add response), you can update its quantity or remove it entirely.

Update quantity (e.g. +/- buttons in your UI)

client.surplus.update(id, { ministock }) replaces the quantity. To implement increment/decrement buttons, fetch the current state first:

Code
import { createKarmaClient } from '@karmalicious/karma-api-js'

const client = createKarmaClient({ apiKey: process.env.KARMA_API_KEY!, locationId: 1234 })

async function adjustSurplusQuantity(surplusId: number, delta: number) {
  const entries = await client.surplus.list()
  const entry = entries.find(e => e.id === surplusId)
  if (!entry) throw new Error(`Surplus entry ${surplusId} not found`)

  const newQuantity = Math.max(0, entry.ministock + delta)

  if (newQuantity === 0) {
    await client.surplus.delete(surplusId)
  } else {
    await client.surplus.update(surplusId, { ministock: newQuantity })
  }
}

Or if you already know the current quantity (e.g. it's displayed in your UI), skip the fetch:

You can also update other fields in the same call — discountPercentage, overridePriceCents, note, validUntil:

Delete a surplus entry

Removes the entry immediately — customers will no longer see it in the app.

Full +/- UI pattern

Here's a complete React example for a surplus management screen with increment, decrement, and delete:

Code
function SurplusRow({ entry, locationId, apiKey, onUpdate }: {
  entry: { id: number; ministock: number; item: { name: string } }
  locationId: number
  apiKey: string
  onUpdate: () => void
}) {
  const update = async (newQty: number) => {
    if (newQty <= 0) {
      await fetch(`/api/proxy/locations/${locationId}/surplus/${entry.id}`, { method: 'DELETE' })
    } else {
      await fetch(`/api/proxy/locations/${locationId}/surplus/${entry.id}`, {
        method: 'PUT',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ ministock: newQty }),
      })
    }
    onUpdate()
  }

  return (
    <div className="surplus-row">
      <span>{entry.item.name}</span>
      <button onClick={() => update(entry.ministock - 1)}>−</button>
      <span>{entry.ministock}</span>
      <button onClick={() => update(entry.ministock + 1)}>+</button>
      <button onClick={() => update(0)}>Remove</button>
    </div>
  )
}

Tip: If quantity reaches 0 in the Karma app (all units sold), the entry becomes inactive automatically — you don't need to delete it. Delete is for manually removing surplus you decide not to sell after all.

MethodEndpointDescription
